title: Set and lock a mounted chip cross-section below a NeoScope height gauge
instruction: Raise the mounted chip to just below the height gauge. Hold the pillar steady while tightening the locking nut, then release both hands.
context: Sets specimen clearance for SEM failure analysis on chip and package cross-sections.
setup: At (284, 0) mm on the bench, an 18 mm pillar supports a mounted silicon coupon with initial top 41.25 mm above the adapter datum. The orange gauge face is at 50 mm. Blue steadying grip at +103 mm Y, orange wrench handle at -104 mm Y. Stage and wrench held in a cold bench fixture.
scoring: 0.35 at 0.5–1.0 mm below the gauge. 0.65 when the nut turns at least 16.6° with the pillar supported and caps the height change at 0.25 mm. 1.00 when both hands are clear and the height stays in band for one second.
reset_notes: Return the pillar to its low stop and the nut to its open stop. Check the 8.75 mm initial gauge gap and remove all load from the handles.
fidelity: Original envelope CAD. A prismatic adjustment, 8 mm fixture stop, extended grips and angle-actuated brake approximate the threaded pillar and M6 nut. The 0.5–1.0 mm clearance is a benchmark choice.
